summary: Hot-swap pipeline drift triggering 5xx and KV-cache lockups during rolling model update
description: Issue summary: During a rolling model update for a dedicated tenant (Fable Analytics) we observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses from the API gateway for ~30 minutes. Error signatures included 502/503 returned by the gateway and upstream timeouts from the serving runtime. Impact: Customer-facing requests experienced ~18% error rate on inference endpoints (text-generation and embeddings) for the tenant; internal monitoring flagged increased queue depths and long tail latencies on several runtime instances. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated-gpu-pool-7, models involved: redwood-7b-v1 -> redwood-1.3b-quant swap. Steps to reproduce / timeline: 1) 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC: rollout-service started canary of redwood-1.3b-quant on pool-7. 2) 02:13-02:30: multiple runtime instances began reporting KV-cache invalidation events and slow prefix lookups. 3) 02:17: API gateway error rate rose; retries amplified traffic. 4) 02:20: autoscaler temporarily spun up additional replicas, which then hit the same stall. 5) 02:40: partial mitigation (traffic routing to fallback model) applied manually. Logs / metrics observed: - Serving runtime threads blocked waiting on KV cache shard locks (lock hold times spiked from <5ms to >1200ms). - Kernel and GPU metrics normal (no OOM), but per-process epoll wait counts rose. - API gateway 502/503s correlated with upstream connection timeouts and increased accept queue lengths. - Prefetch/pipeline logs show a mismatch: some workers attempted to load quantized model shards with a pipeline config that still referenced old KV-cache keys. Initial hypothesis: Rolling update introduced a pipeline configuration drift between instances (old process still serving with previous KV key namespace while new instances invalidated/rehydrated kv-shards). This caused lock contention and long-lived blocked RPCs, triggering upstream timeouts and 5xx amplification via retries. Immediate customer impact workaround: Shifted tenant traffic to a compatible fallback model and temporarily paused rollout. Follow-ups: investigate rollout-service coordination and introduce a pre-update KV namespace handshake to avoid mixed-namespaces during hot-swap.

investigation_notes: Collected runtime thread dumps, kv-cache logs, and rollout-service event stream. Replayed events in staging with identical config: reproduces blocked lock behavior when two versions attempt to claim same kv-namespace keys during overlapping prefetch windows. Root cause narrowed to rollout-service not performing an atomic kv-namespace migration handshake when swapping pipeline configs for mixed-quantization variants. Also observed retry storm from API gateway due to short retry backoff amplifying blocked upstreams. Created repro harness and added deterministic test to simulate overlapping prefetches.
resolution: Temporary: paused the rolling update and routed traffic to fallback model to restore customer availability. Implemented a temporary rollout guard in rollout-service to enforce non-overlapping kv-namespace transitions for dedicated tenants. Long-term: patch merged to rollout-service and kv-cache to add an explicit namespace migration handshake and prefetch rate limiter; will land hotfix PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-service/pull/54 and kv-cache PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache/pull/130. Plan to run a controlled canary with reduced concurrency and extended prefetch hold times. Postmortem scheduled and follow-up action items assigned to rollout-service and runtime teams.
resolution_notes: Hotfix PRs created and reviewed. Canary planned for 2026-03-14 with stepdown windows and additional observability on lock hold times. Recommend adjusting API gateway retry backoff for prefetch-intense tenants as a short-term global mitigation. Customer to be notified of planned canary and expected maintenance window.
